stem:
Which of the following statements about Subhas Chandra Bose are correct?
1. He was elected President of the Indian National Congress at Tripuri session of 1938 A.D.
2. He escaped from home internment in January 1941
A.D.
3. On October 21st 1943 A.D. he constituted the Provincial Governmert of India in Singapore.
expl: In 1938, the 51st annual session of the Congress was held at Haripura (Gujarat), not at Tripuri. Subhas Chandra Bose presided over the Haripura session. The 52nd annual session of the Congress was held at Tripuri (M.P.) in 1939, and it was also presided over by Subhas Chandra Bose. However, later he resigned from this post. Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose successfully carried out the plan to escape from his house at night in disguise and leave Calcutta in January 1941. He formed the Provincial Government of India in Singapore on 21 October 1943.

Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23 January 1897 in Cuttack, Odisha. In 1919, he obtained the degree of graduation from Scottish Church College, affiliated to Calcutta University, and in 1920 he passed the Indian Civil Service (I.C.S.) examination. He became the President of the Indian National Congress at Haripura in 1938 and at Tripuri in 1939. In 1939, he resigned from the Congress presidentship and founded the Forward Bloc, and in 1941 he went to Germany. In 1943, he took command of the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army). He is commonly remembered as “Netaji”. The title/address “Netaji” was given to Subhas Chandra Bose by the Free India Legion (Indian Free Legion) of Indian soldiers stationed in Germany.

stem: Who assumed the command of the Indian National Army and gave famous battle cry, 'Chalo Delhi'?
expl: The initial formation of the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army—INA) took place during the Second World War with Japan’s support. In the early phase, Captain Mohan Singh and Ras Bihari Bose played an important role in its organisation, but later its leadership came into the hands of Subhas Chandra Bose. He organised the Azad Hind Fauj and gave the famous slogan “Chalo Delhi”.

stem: In which year was the Indian National Army founded?
expl: In practical terms, as a military unit, the Indian National Army (another name—Azad Hind Fauj) was formed on 15 July 1942 under the leadership of Captain Mohan Singh, while the Bangkok Conference resolutions of June 1942 paved the way for the formation of the INA (Indian National Army). It is noteworthy that Indian residents in the Malaya region formed a political organisation named the “All Malaya Indian Independence League”. Rash Bihari Bose was invited to preside over it. In the Bangkok Conference held in June 1942, a proposal was made to form a “Council of Action” and a “Representative Committee”, which was entrusted with the responsibility of coordination and supervision between the “Indian Independence League” and the “Indian National Army”. Rash Behari Bose was made the Chairman of the Council of Action, while K. P. K. Menon and Nedyam Raghavan were civilian members, and Mohan Singh and Gilani were military members. Due to ideological differences with the Japanese, Mohan Singh announced the dissolution of the INA in December 1942; however, Rash Behari Bose removed Mohan Singh from his post. Later, Mohan Singh was arrested by the Japanese army. The leadership of the INA was handed over by Rash Bihari Bose to the great leader Subhas Chandra Bose. Two days after reaching Singapore, on 4 July 1943, Subhas Chandra Bose assumed the leadership of the Indian National Army. For convenience, it is also called the Second Indian National Army. In Hindi, we know it as the “Azad Hind Fauj.”

stem: Where was Azad Hind Fauj set up in 1943?
expl: The Azad Hind Fauj was reorganized in 1943 on the island of Singapore under the leadership of Subhas Chandra Bose; however, at that time Singapore was under Japanese control (from 1942 to 1945). Before Japanese occupation, Singapore was a part of British Malaya (Malaya).

stem: In October 1943, Subhas Chandra Bose set up a provisional government of Free India which was recognized by how many countries including Japan?
expl: In October 1943, during the Second World War, the Provisional Government of Azad Hind (Provisional Government of Free India) established by Subhas Chandra Bose was recognized by nine countries. These were mainly Axis powers and Japan-backed regimes. The list of recognizing countries is as follows- 1. Japan, 2. Germany (Nazi regime), 3. Italy, 4. Thailand (Siam), 5. Burma/Myanmar (Japan-supported government), 6. Philippines (Second Republic sponsored by Japan), 7. Manchukuo (Japanese puppet government in Manchuria, China), 8. Wang Jingwei regime (Nanjing, China—Japanese puppet government), and 9. Croatia (a puppet government supported by powers). Some sources mention Slovakia or some other Axis-associated country, but the widely accepted number is nine. However, these recognitions were largely symbolic. Note- The Wang Jingwei regime is also called the Nationalist China or China (Nanking/Nanjing) regime.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: During the Second World War (1939–45), the Andaman and Nicobar Islands slipped out of British control and came under Japanese occupation in 1942. Japan’s control remained till 1945, when the British reoccupied the islands. In November 1943, the Japanese government symbolically handed over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to Subhas Chandra Bose’s Azad Hind Provisional Government of Free India (Provisional Government of Free India). After receiving this charge, Netaji renamed Nicobar as “Swaraj” and Andaman as “Shaheed”.
